title: Acts and the letters, looking back
hookLine: Lydia, Priscilla, Paul's chains, faith, hope, love
tomorrow: whose voice do you follow when everyone has advice?

cards: An envelope in the mailbox with your name in someone's own handwriting. It lands differently than a text. The first churches in Acts didn't meet in church buildings.
They met in houses, and they were held together by letters, read aloud and passed along. Some of those letters still carry a trace of the hands that wrote them.

teach.b: Start with a house. By a riverbank, Paul meets Lydia, "a seller of purple", "whose heart the Lord opened". She's baptized with her household and insists Paul's group stay at her home, and later the believers gather there.
Paul greets two tentmakers, Priscilla and Aquila, who risked their necks for him, and adds, "Likewise greet the church that is in their house." A church, in a house. Now the paper.
One to tell a friend tonight: at the end of Romans, the man holding the pen says hello.
"I Tertius, who wrote this epistle, salute you in the Lord." Then, in Galatians, Paul takes the pen himself: "Ye see how large a letter I have written unto you with mine own hand."
And Colossians closes with his signature and a request: "The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds." A man signing his name in chains.
To a quarreling church in Corinth, he wrote the line that holds the rest: "And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity."
In that chapter of the King James, charity means love, the kind that suffers long and is kind, not a donation. Faith keeps you going. Hope looks ahead.
Love is what's still standing when the quarrel is over.

how: Churches read Paul's letters aloud in worship, and 1 Corinthians 13, with faith, hope and love, is a reading some couples choose for their weddings.

games.q: what does “acts and the letters” mean?
o: the early church in homes, held together by Paul's letters
the stories of Jesus's childhood in Nazareth
the laws Moses gave Israel, collected into one book

games.q: Acts and the letters — tap the pairs.

s: the first churches in Acts met in their own church buildings
they met in homes: Lydia's, and Priscilla and Aquila's ('the church that is in their house').
Romans names the man who wrote the letter down
'I Tertius, who wrote this epistle, salute you in the Lord' (Romans 16:22).
'charity' in 1 Corinthians 13 (King James) means giving money
in that chapter it means love: the kind that suffers long and is kind.

games.q: a friend starts a Bible study with five people in her apartment. her cousin says it's not a "real" church. what does the text give her?
o: nothing: a church needs a building and a pastor first.
Paul greets 'the church that is in their house.'
only a Sunday-morning meeting counts as church.
games.why: churches define 'a church' in different ways, but the letters greet whole churches meeting in homes, like Priscilla and Aquila's (Romans 16:5).

practice: Find paper and a pen, and write a few lines by hand to someone who held you together on this road: a thank-you, a memory, one plain word of love. Feel the pen move, and let your handwriting be yours, crooked or not.
You don't have to send it today.

wordCard.voice: Acts and the letters. A church in homes and riverbanks and prison cells, held together by paper, and by faith, hope and love.

orig.note: Greek: love. in 1 Corinthians 13:13 the King James gives it as charity.

carryVoice: Your line: the greatest is love. The King James calls it charity, the love that suffers long and is kind. Go gently.
